Definition: from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle (compare G427)) and G127; impudence, i.e. (by implication) importunity:--importunity.
BiblicalUsage: The word is used once only, in the parable of the friend at midnight: though the man will not rise and give him bread because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth. Importunity is shameless persistence — knocking until the door opens, not because the friendship demands it but because the asking will not stop.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for shameless asking carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the parable — the friend who keeps knocking until he is heard.
